### D.3 Athena: Action-level evaluation prompt

The first stage of behaviour-level evolution, Eval, scores Branchus’s
trajectory one *action* at a time: each step is attributed to the single
role that produced it (one of scheduler, planner, searcher, reasoner,
critic) and judged in isolation against that role’s rubric, with the
resolved outcome $`y_{q}`$ withheld so that the judgement reflects the
*process* rather than the outcome (Section
[4.4](#S4.SS4 "4.4 Athena: Recursive Evolution System ‣ 4 Approach ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")).
The driver (main.py) dispatches each step to the matching template:
Prompt
[D.3](#A4.SS3 "D.3 Athena: Action-level evaluation prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
is the worker-step judge, while the scheduler is instead judged over its
full decision trace. Every step is scored independently by each judge
model in the ensemble, and the per-dimension verdicts are aggregated by
their median. The {{role}}, {{dimensions}}, and {{rubric}} fields are
specialized per role. These per-action scores and observed_issues are
the input to the extraction stage of Appendix
[D.4](#A4.SS4 "D.4 Athena: Skill Extraction Prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting").

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### D.4 Athena: Skill Extraction Prompt

Given the per-action evaluation of Appendix
[D.3](#A4.SS3 "D.3 Athena: Action-level evaluation prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting"),
Extract distils the surviving experience — a non-obvious action that
helped or a recurring trap — from the trajectory, Filter discards weak
candidates, and Organize then grades each experience into one
role-specific four-level skill $`s=(s_{1},s_{2},s_{3},s_{4})`$ (Section
[4.4](#S4.SS4 "4.4 Athena: Recursive Evolution System ‣ 4 Approach ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")).
The concrete procedure actually applied in the trajectory is kept
verbatim as the most concrete level, and the levels above it generalize
that procedure step by step — first to the question type, then within
the broader domain, and finally to a cross-domain principle — giving the
schema ordered from abstract ($`s_{1}`$) to concrete ($`s_{4}`$). The
case study of Appendix
[E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 Athena: The Distilled Skill ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
shows both artifacts: the raw extracted experience (Prompt
[E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 Athena: The Distilled Skill ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting"))
and the graded four-level skill it becomes (Prompt
[E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 Athena: The Distilled Skill ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")).
Prompt
[D.4](#A4.SS4 "D.4 Athena: Skill Extraction Prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
shows the grading template; the {{role}} and {{role_contract}} fields
bind the skill to one role’s responsibility and its allowed and
forbidden actions, and the {{experience}} and {{evidence_packet}} fields
carry the extracted experience together with the trajectory evidence
that supports it.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### D.5 Athena: Environment-Level Skill Synthesis Prompt

Environment-level evolution converts Branchus’s error profile
$`\rho^{(t)}`$ (Equation
([12](#S4.E12 "Equation 12 ‣ 4.4 Athena: Recursive Evolution System ‣ 4 Approach ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")))
into task-synthesis skills
$`\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{env}}=\textsc{Synthesize}(\rho^{(t)})`$ that
steer Prometheus toward harder, weakness-targeted questions (Section
[4.4](#S4.SS4 "4.4 Athena: Recursive Evolution System ‣ 4 Approach ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")).
Prompt
[D.5](#A4.SS5 "D.5 Athena: Environment-Level Skill Synthesis Prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
shows the synthesis template; the resulting skills are injected into the
{{synthesis_skills}} field of the Prometheus prompt (Prompt
[D.1](#A4.SS1 "D.1 Prometheus: Question Synthesis Prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")).

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Appendix E Case Study

To make the recursive self-improvement loop concrete, this section walks
through a single worked example in the order the three modules act
within one round: we first show how Prometheus synthesizes a forecasting
question, contrasting a draft produced before environment-level
optimization with the sharper, weakness-targeted draft produced after a
task-synthesis skill is applied (Appendix
[E.1](#A5.SS1 "E.1 Prometheus: Skill-Conditioned Question Synthesis ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting"));
we then show how Branchus forecasts such a question, tracing the search
and predict teams through to a probabilistic answer (Appendix
[E.2](#A5.SS2 "E.2 Branchus: A Worked Prediction ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting"));
and finally we show the reusable skill that Athena distils from that
trajectory (Appendix
[E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 Athena: The Distilled Skill ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")).
Together these snapshots illustrate how the products of one round — a
sharper question, a trajectory, and a skill — become the raw materials
of the next.

### E.1 Prometheus: Skill-Conditioned Question Synthesis

We first show how the *same* crawled source material yields different
questions before and after environment-level optimization. The two
drafts below are drawn from a controlled comparison in which we ran the
question-synthesis pipeline over an identical corpus of calendars and
feeds twice: once with the baseline generator and once after a
task-synthesis skill from $`\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{env}}`$ (Appendix
[D.5](#A4.SS5 "D.5 Athena: Environment-Level Skill Synthesis Prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting"))
is injected into the {{synthesis_skills}} field of the Prometheus prompt
(Prompt
[D.1](#A4.SS1 "D.1 Prometheus: Question Synthesis Prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")).
The two batches resolve to the same underlying events, which lets us
read the effect of the skill directly: for a given event, the baseline
generator fans out over many predicates and tends to retain the easy,
nearly-decided ones (“who wins”, a coarse category band), whereas the
skill-steered generator is more selective and keeps the sharp,
weakness-targeted predicate — typically a *numerical forecast* or a
*threshold judgment*, two of the categories on which Branchus’s error
profile $`\rho^{(t)}`$ (Equation
([12](#S4.E12 "Equation 12 ‣ 4.4 Athena: Recursive Evolution System ‣ 4 Approach ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")))
is highest. Quantitatively, the skill-steered batch emits fewer
questions per event ($`1.29`$ vs. $`2.15`$ on the shared events) and
concentrates them on these harder predicates, rather than padding the
batch with low-information rephrasings. Prompt
[E.1](#A5.SS1 "E.1 Prometheus: Skill-Conditioned Question Synthesis ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
shows a baseline draft produced without any task-synthesis guidance;
Prompt
[E.1](#A5.SS1 "E.1 Prometheus: Skill-Conditioned Question Synthesis ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
shows the draft produced once the skill is applied, illustrating how
environment-level evolution sharpens the question toward Branchus’s
weaknesses while preserving objectivity and reproducible resolvability.
All questions are synthesized in Chinese; we translate them here for
presentation, preserving the original sources, reference series, and
resolution rules.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

A second example, drawn from a different domain in the same comparison,
shows the sharpening is not specific to sports. From the identical
source — the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) daily AQI bulletin
for Delhi, whose preceding seven days read
$`118,160,169,178,154,145,78`$ — the baseline generator asks for the
coarse air-quality *category* (a three-way band of “0–100 / 101–200 /
201+”), which the recent trend already pins to “Moderate” with
near-certainty; the skill-steered generator instead asks for the exact
integer *Index Value* published in that day’s bulletin, a numerical
forecast with a precise ground truth and a reliable public resolution
source. In both examples the environment-level skill holds the source
material, the objectivity, and the reproducible resolvability fixed, and
moves only the *difficulty* of the question into the category where
Branchus is weakest.

### E.2 Branchus: A Worked Prediction

We next trace Branchus on a question posed by Prometheus, such as the
skill-steered weightlifting total of Prompt
[E.1](#A5.SS1 "E.1 Prometheus: Skill-Conditioned Question Synthesis ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting").
The search team decomposes the question, gathers and critiques evidence,
and hands a structured evidence summary to the predict team, which
reconciles the evidence into a calibrated probability, recording the
full trajectory
$`\tau=(\{\tau_{\mathrm{s}}^{(j)}\}_{j},\tau_{\mathrm{p}})`$. To make
the two evolution channels of Athena concrete, we show Branchus
forecasting the *same* question under three configurations: Prompt
[E.2](#A5.SS2 "E.2 Branchus: A Worked Prediction ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
is the baseline, before any evolution; Prompt
[E.2](#A5.SS2 "E.2 Branchus: A Worked Prediction ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
adds the distilled skill of Appendix
[E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 Athena: The Distilled Skill ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
to the retrieved skill set, illustrating behaviour-level evolution
($`\Phi_{\mathrm{skill}}`$) without touching the weights; and Prompt
[E.2](#A5.SS2 "E.2 Branchus: A Worked Prediction ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")
uses the predict-team weights after RFT, illustrating parameter-level
evolution ($`\Phi_{\mathrm{rl}}`$). Holding the question fixed isolates
the effect of each channel on the trajectory and the resulting
prediction.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### E.3 Athena: The Distilled Skill

Finally, from the trajectory above, Athena’s behaviour-level operator
$`\Phi_{\mathrm{skill}}`$ turns the evaluated trajectory into a reusable
skill. First, Eval judges the process one action at a time with the
outcome withheld (Appendix
[D.3](#A4.SS3 "D.3 Athena: Action-level evaluation prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting"));
then Extract and Filter distil the surviving experience — a single
non-obvious action that helped — as a raw, unlevelled record (Prompt
[E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 Athena: The Distilled Skill ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting"));
and finally Organize grades that experience into the four-level schema
$`s=(s_{1},s_{2},s_{3},s_{4})`$ of Section
[4.4](#S4.SS4 "4.4 Athena: Recursive Evolution System ‣ 4 Approach ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting"),
keeping the concrete procedure verbatim as $`s_{4}`$ and generalizing it
upward (Prompt
[E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 Athena: The Distilled Skill ‣ Appendix E Case Study ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting")).
The extraction and grading templates are those of Appendix
[D.4](#A4.SS4 "D.4 Athena: Skill Extraction Prompt ‣ Appendix D Prompt Templates ‣ Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting").
